passage:
The school began playing soft music during lunch. The principal hoped it would make the cafeteria calmer.
On the first day, students talked over the music and did not notice it. On the second day, the volume was raised, but then it became annoying.
Finally, the music club chose quieter songs and played them at a lower volume. The goal was not to make students listen, but to make the room feel less noisy.
After a week, teachers found that students shouted less.
The music did not solve every cafeteria problem, but it helped.
A good background does not need to be the center of attention. Sometimes it works best when people barely notice it.
